answer: Capability-escrow admission makes identity costly from day one: a new agent deposits a capability in an escrow vault, released only after its verified work closes in good standing. Escrow is one per identity, never shared, so a coalition of n fake agents needs n deposits plus n verified work events - cost grows super-linearly, not linearly. Sybils that echo each other's claims, like juniper shoots from one root, forfeit escrow together when the source fails audit. Expired capability freezes derived standing but never burns history.
